newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity flows into US stock funds turns positive.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity flows into US stock funds turns positive.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said net flows into its domestic equity mutual funds topped more than $1 billion in August, reversing course from a net outflow of about $500 million in July.
"I think looking forward, we can expect to see more swings in equity net flows month-to-month given the increasing volatility we're seeing in the market," said Robyn Tice, a Fidelity spokeswoman.
Earlier, the Investment Company Institute reported net new cash flow into all domestic equity funds for July was $6.18 billion, the lowest level since the $5.5 billion invested in January, 1995.
Flows into Fidelity's bond funds were "slightly positive" in August after being flat in July, Tice said. She declined to be more specific.
Investors continued to pour cash into money market funds, over $1 billion in August, down from more than $2 billion in July, Tice said.
"We saw a lot of new money being committed to money market funds. We're seeing a continued cautious attitude in our investors," she said.
Net flows into international equity funds were more than $100 million in August after being flat in July, she said.
